ai.description: This snake reaches 30–40 cm. It is dark brown or purplish with yellow-spotted sides and a blunt, shield-like tail. Large, smooth scales cover its cylindrical body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis macrolepis* is best distinguished by its large, smooth, hexagonal scales on the posterior body and a distinct, shield-like tail ending in a rough, naked disc.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis macrolepis* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Bombay earth snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil to forage for earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis macrolepis* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis macrolepis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Kerala at mid-to-high elevations.
